A small, discreet prompt that is easily dismissable might solve this.

When a user tries to comment, have the prompt ask them to vote or simply ignore the message.

Have two/three buttons under the comment box.

''Comment with an upvote'' and ''Comment with a downvote'' and ''Dismiss''.

Or simply ''Up'' ''Down'' and ''Sumbit''. The latter not affecting vote weight. All are submit buttons.

I'm not a fan of either options given in the OP.

Option 1 is a prompt. Unless it's an error, prompts are generally bad practice. If you constantly prompt a user they will get annoyed and eventually stop/leave. I feel introducing prompts would quickly kill the community. Not many people want to be bothered by a constant stream of prompts.

Option 2 is definitely the better of the two options since it's less intrusive. I just don't agree with every topic requiring my vote. Just because I comment, doesn't mean it deserves an upvote or downvote. I wouldn't want to have to keep checking "Dismiss" every time I comment.
